notes:
Top-level summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS evaluating Redwood Hosted API as initial quick win, now negotiating Dedicated reserved capacity. Customer priority = predictable unit economics + strict latency SLOs.

POC notes: Hosted API results encouraging for retrieval+rerank (embeddings pipeline), but tail latency spikes on high-concurrency synthetic test. Dedicated POC showed 25-35% cost improvement vs hosted for batch ingestion flows; chat p95 improved but not below customer's 200ms target in default config.

Requirements (customer language / shorthand):
- Workloads: user-facing chat (primary), support agent assistant, product doc search, reranking for recommendations.
- Latency: target p95 <= 250ms (VP Eng: "can't risk >200-250ms for live chat").
- Throughput: anticipated steady-state 30-50 rps for chat endpoints; bursts up to 120 rps during peak features launch.
- Cost sensitivity: aiming to reduce per-token inference cost ~30% vs current OpenAI spend; procurement focused on predictable monthly burn.
- Models: prefer Llama2 / open variants; open to quantized 70B/30B variants if quality holds. Wants guidance on quantization profiles from Redwood Optimize.

Pricing/packaging negotiation points discussed:
- Commit levels: customer prefers 3-tier commit ramp (initial commit = 4 reserved GPU-equivalent, 90-day ramp to 8, 12-month steady state at 12) — Redwood pricing to include ramp discounts.
notes_continued:
- Burst: require guaranteed burst pool of +30% above committed capacity for 15 min windows; billing preference = included burst minutes per month with soft throttling after threshold.
- Overage: customer requests capped overage multiplier (no more than 1.5x committed rate for next 6 months) and clear invoice-level breakdown by token, GPU-hours, and burst usage.
- Ramp schedule: formal 90-day ramp with quarterly checkpoints and optional early top-up if product launch accelerates.
- Credits & incentives: asked for a time-limited ramp credit for first 3 months to offset migration dev costs.

Security/compliance:
- SSO/SAML integration required for ops console; Redwood must provide KMS integration pattern (customer uses AWS KMS + GCP KMS for multi-cloud).
- Data residency: primary AZ in US-East for prod, EU region for EU customers; legal want a clause about no model training on customer data.

Quotes and behavioral notes:
- VP Eng (S. Ortega): "We need a clear fall-back plan — if dedicated node fails, route to hosted-but-throttled model; we can't afford complete outage."
- Head of ML (D. Li): asked for quantization QA and accuracy drift metrics during canary.
- Procurement: pushing for a single-line item committed spend with monthly true-up vs the per-token model.

Next steps (short):
- AE to deliver revised Dedicated proposal (commit tiers + burst appendix + sample invoices) by 2026-03-12.
- SE to provide quantization/latency playbook and expected p95 projections for chosen model variants by 2026-03-10.
- Legal to receive SOC2 artifacts and proposed MSA redlines (customer to send standard Data Processing Addendum).

Open questions / blockers (customer stated):
- How exactly is burst billed when reserved capacity is exhausted? formula clarified but needs example invoice.
- Need a guaranteed SLA for dedicated latency tiers (p95) — Redwood to propose workable SLO+credits.
- Procurement wants a 12-month commitment discount table vs month-to-month and clear ramp termination terms.
